newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Trade in Belgian Spector suspended on issue report.
newsitem.headline: Trade in Belgian Spector suspended on issue report.

text.p: Trade in shares of Belgium's Spector Photo Group NV, Europe's second-largest photo processing group, was suspended on Thursday following a newspaper report on a planned capital increase.
"We have decided...and the company has agreed, that trading will remain suspended until Monday," a Brussels bourse official told Reuters.
Financial daily De Financieel-Economische Tijd said Spector was planning a one billion franc capital increase in October to finance recent acquisitions abroad.

Last month Spector said it signed a definitive agreement to acquire a majority stake in Porst, a Swiss photo group with operations in Germany and Hungary, and a 100 percent stake in Interdiscount Francefrom Swiss group Interdiscount.
Interdiscount meanwhile has changed its name to Distefora.

The Belgian group said at the time that agreement remained "conditional to the confirmation of the financing for the acquisition and to an agreement regarding the financial restructuring of Interdiscount France with its creditors."
Spector said in a statement on Thursday that it "does not deny" plans for a capital increase.

But it added that "Spector and (its controlling shareholder) Fotoinvest firmly deny the connection between the acquisitions of Interdiscount France and Porst Holding AG, as represented in the article of De Financieel-Economische Tijd of today."
A Spector spokesman declined to clarify the statement, and told Reuters further information would be given at a news conference on Friday.
